subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which year did Napoleon Bonaparte seize power in the coup of 18-19 Brumaire?
questions.explain: Napoleon overthrew the Directory in the coup of Brumaire (9-10 November 1799), establishing the Consulate with himself as First Consul.

questions.q: In which year did Mussolini lead the March on Rome that brought him to power?
questions.explain: The Fascist March on Rome of October 1922 prompted King Victor Emmanuel III to appoint Mussolini Prime Minister.

questions.q: What 1947 US policy pledged support to nations resisting communism?
questions.explain: The Truman Doctrine of 1947 promised aid to free peoples resisting subjugation, starting with Greece and Turkey.

questions.q: What was abolished by the National Assembly's decrees of 4-11 August 1789?
questions.explain: On the night of 4 August 1789 the Assembly abolished feudal privileges and seigneurial dues, dismantling the legal framework of the ancien regime.

questions.q: What was the popular name for the European Recovery Program of 1947-48?
questions.explain: The Marshall Plan provided US economic aid to rebuild Western Europe and resist communism.

questions.q: The fall and execution of Robespierre, ending the Terror, occurred in which month and year?
questions.explain: Robespierre was overthrown in the Thermidorian Reaction and guillotined on 28 July 1794 (10 Thermidor Year II).

questions.q: The Brezhnev Doctrine asserted the right to do what?
options: Intervene in any socialist state threatening communism
questions.explain: The Brezhnev Doctrine (1968) claimed the right to intervene to protect socialism in bloc states.

questions.q: Polish independence from communism was spearheaded by which trade union movement?
questions.explain: Solidarity, led by Lech Walesa, drove Poland's break from communist rule by 1989.

questions.q: Who led the communist victory in China in 1949?
questions.explain: Mao Zedong's Communists won the civil war and proclaimed the People's Republic of China in October 1949.

questions.q: Which Soviet economic body answered the Marshall Plan?
questions.explain: Comecon (1949) coordinated the economies of the Soviet bloc as a counter to Marshall aid.

questions.q: In which year did Fascist Italy invade Abyssinia (Ethiopia)?
questions.explain: Italy invaded Abyssinia in October 1935, completing its conquest in 1936 and provoking League of Nations sanctions.

questions.q: In which year were the Yalta and Potsdam conferences held?
questions.explain: Both the Yalta (February) and Potsdam (July-August) conferences took place in 1945.

questions.q: The ideological and political division of Europe after 1945 between Western and Soviet spheres became known as the:
questions.explain: Churchill popularised the phrase 'Iron Curtain' in 1946 to describe the Soviet-imposed division of Europe during the Cold War.

questions.q: At which 1187 battle did Saladin annihilate the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem?
questions.explain: At the Battle of Hattin (4 July 1187) Saladin destroyed the Frankish field army, leaving the kingdom defenceless.

questions.q: The murder of which socialist deputy in 1924 provoked a major crisis for Mussolini's regime?
questions.explain: The kidnapping and murder of Giacomo Matteotti in June 1924, after he denounced Fascist violence, triggered the Matteotti Crisis.

questions.q: The Byzantine defeat at which 1071 battle helped prompt the appeal that led to the First Crusade?
questions.explain: The Seljuk Turks crushed the Byzantines at Manzikert in 1071, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement and prompting the appeal to the West.

questions.q: Which 1979 event helped trigger the 'Second Cold War'?
options: The fall of the Berlin Wall
questions.explain: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979 ended detente and heightened tensions.

questions.q: Which two reform policies are most associated with Gorbachev?
questions.explain: Gorbachev pursued glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring).

questions.q: Which Christian city did the Fourth Crusade sack in 1204?
questions.explain: Diverted from the Holy Land, the Fourth Crusade sacked the Byzantine capital Constantinople in April 1204.

questions.q: What 1968 reform movement did the Warsaw Pact crush in Czechoslovakia?
questions.explain: The Prague Spring's liberal reforms under Dubcek were ended by a Warsaw Pact invasion in August 1968.

questions.q: In which year was Louis XVI executed by guillotine?
questions.explain: Convicted of treason by the National Convention, Louis XVI was guillotined on 21 January 1793.

questions.q: In which year did Italy join the First World War, declaring war on Austria-Hungary?
questions.explain: Italy entered the war on the Entente side in May 1915 after the secret Treaty of London promised territorial gains.

questions.q: Which two leaders confronted each other during the Cuban Missile Crisis?
questions.explain: President Kennedy and Soviet leader Khrushchev faced off over missiles in Cuba in 1962.

questions.q: Which English king was a leading commander of the Third Crusade?
questions.explain: Richard I ('the Lionheart') led the Third Crusade (1189-92), recapturing Acre and negotiating a truce with Saladin.

questions.q: Which Italian maritime republic played the dominant role in diverting the Fourth Crusade?
questions.explain: Venice, under Doge Enrico Dandolo, supplied the fleet and redirected the crusade first to Zara and then to Constantinople.

questions.q: At which 1815 battle was Napoleon finally defeated, ending his Hundred Days?
questions.explain: Napoleon was decisively defeated at Waterloo on 18 June 1815 by Wellington and Blucher, leading to his exile to St Helena.

questions.q: In which years did the Berlin Blockade and Airlift take place?
questions.explain: The Berlin Blockade ran from June 1948 to May 1949, countered by the Western airlift.

questions.q: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
questions.explain: The Berlin Wall was erected in August 1961 to halt the flow of refugees to the West.

questions.q: Which ideology, emphasising class struggle and the abolition of private property, drew on the writings of Karl Marx?
questions.explain: Communism, rooted in Marx's analysis of class conflict, sought a classless society through the abolition of private property.

questions.q: In which year did US combat troops complete withdrawal from Vietnam?
questions.explain: Under the 1973 Paris Peace Accords, US combat forces withdrew from Vietnam.
